findings.text: the _deferred_run_ids docstring tells a caller that "a caller that composes the line for a moment composes the deferral for the same moment", but the reader it dispatches to, obligations._acknowledgements_in_force, honours the passed instant only for a live pointer: for a promoted run it delegates to runs.recorded_promoted_acknowledgements, which compares each recorded deadline against runs._deferral_clock() (the real clock) and never sees the moment. Not reachable in production, where every call site composes for now, so it is a false uniformity claim in new documentation rather than a live defect.

verdicts.assertions: test_a_deferred_run_leaves_the_line_until_its_instant asserts deferred-node absent at now and one second before the instant and present exactly once after it, beside the positive control that expired-node is present throughout; test_the_line_reads_the_obligations_deferral_reader injects a deferral visible only in a monkeypatched reader and requires the run to vanish, so it fails if needs_you stops dispatching through that reader. Reinstating the regression (the declared mutation, deferred = frozenset()) reddens both cases at EXIT=1 in logs/negative-control.txt, so the assertions are independent of the values under test rather than moving with them.

verdicts.done_when: the done_when requires the deferral be read through obligations._acknowledgements_in_force with obligations.py untouched, a three-case test in a temporary home, two git-checkout arms with the four follower variables unset under pytest -n 8, lone-id repeats, the module-window test green and a ruff delta against the base blobs; the manifest records all of these and logs/gate-base.txt, logs/gate-head.txt, logs/negative-control.txt, logs/one-arm-repeat-base.txt and logs/one-arm-repeat-head.txt carry them.
